# Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is CoreCoin and how does it work?**
A: CoreCoin (CORE) is a decentralized Layer-1 digital asset operating on a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) blockchain. It enables peer-to-peer value transfer without intermediaries, supports smart contracts, and allows users to maintain custody of their assets. Transactions are recorded on a public, tamper-resistant ledger.

**Q: What is the maximum supply of CoreCoin?**
A: The maximum supply of CoreCoin is 2,000,000,000 CORE. This supply cap is fixed and cannot be altered without community governance approval.

**Q: How fast are CoreCoin transactions?**
A: CoreCoin has an average block time of ~5 seconds, with transaction finality typically achieved in ~10 seconds under normal network conditions. Both metrics may vary with network load.

**Q: Can I stake CoreCoin to earn rewards?**
A: Yes, CoreCoin supports staking. Users can lock tokens to support network security, with rewards dependent on network conditions. Staking periods, minimum thresholds, and reward rates are variable and defined by protocol governance. Rewards are not guaranteed.

**Q: How are CoreCoin transactions secured?**
A: CoreCoin uses cryptographic signatures (ECDSA or Ed25519) for transaction validation and SHA-3 hashing. The network is secured through distributed validator participation, with staking allowing users to contribute to security. Third-party audits are conducted for protocol integrity.

**Q: Can I recover my CoreCoin if I lose my private keys?**
A: No. CoreCoin operates on a self-custody model with no third-party key recovery. Users are solely responsible for securely storing private keys. Loss of private keys results in permanent loss of funds.

**Q: Does CoreCoin support smart contracts?**
A: Yes. CoreCoin supports smart contracts through a PoS-compatible virtual machine (VM). This enables developers to build decentralized applications (DApps) and programmable contracts on the network.
